items.title: Hate generative AI? Maybe it's time to boycott Netflix
items.excerpt: With Netflix leaning into generative AI across production, Creative Bloq argues creatives angry about AI's encroachment should vote with their subscriptions — a look at how a major studio's gen-AI adoption reshapes the creative industry.

items.title: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5 for both AI coding and general office work
items.excerpt: Anthropic's new frontier model Claude Opus 5 is a cheaper, stronger model for coding and agents — the class of model that now powers AI design tools like Claude Design, Cursor, Lovable and Figma Make, so its release ripples directly into designers' AI workflows.

items.title: When generation is free, taste is everything
items.excerpt: GoodBarber's Mathieu Poli argues that as generative AI makes execution free and infinite, a designer's real value shifts to taste and judgment — the one thing the machine can't supply. A designer-facing take on where craft still matters in an AI workflow.

items.title: I turned a photo of my handwriting into a real font, then open-sourced the whole pipeline
items.excerpt: A designer photographed a single page of handwritten letters in dim light and ran an open-sourced pipeline that outputs an installable TTF — a hands-on look at AI-assisted type design and how far automated font generation has come.

items.title: Character Consistency Across 24 Pages of a Generated Picture Book
items.excerpt: Generating one AI illustration of a child from a reference photo is easy now; keeping that same character consistent across 24 pages is the hard part. A practical walkthrough of character-consistency techniques for generative illustration and design workflows.
